text: The following question stood in the name of  Mr Kok Heng Leun –  12 To ask	the Minister for Health whether the Ministry will consider giving Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) holders who are married to Singapore Citizens, similar health subsidies as LTVP-Plus holders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This is the general principle which applies to different types of Government subsidies, including for healthcare services.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can I just have a quick supplementary question?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What are the criteria which the Ministry is using in justifying a subsidy for LTVP-Plus, but not LTVP?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, there is a differentiation in terms of the benefits of these two categories, including subsidies for healthcare services.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Sorry if I did not make myself clear.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Just wanted to know what are the criteria that make the Ministry decide on giving that to the LTVP-Plus, but not the LTVP.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: There must be some form of criteria, because both are LTVPs − one has Plus and one has no Plus.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: There must be some form of criteria that motivates the decision.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Between the two categories, there will be a differentiation in terms of the benefits for these two groups.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Just one supplementary question for the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The Minister of State alluded to the cost factor.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Has the Government actually done a study on quantifying what will be the cost impact if this benefit was extended to LTVP spouses of Singaporeans, beyond just the LTVP-Plus?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think that question is not part of the original question, so if the Member would like more information, he can file a separate Parliamentary Question.
